title: Whole Numbers on the Number Line

stageA.sourceCopyright: Illustrative Mathematics/Kendall Hunt 2021, CC BY 4.0; branded marks excluded
stageA.goal: Use points and ticks on an equally spaced number line to show whole numbers as lengths from zero; 2.MD.B.6
stageA.warmup: Original Notice and Wonder compares a number line with ruler marked 0..12; students discuss how same-spaced ticks and position from zero work
stageA.activity1: Original ten-unit number lines: fill blank ticks with consecutive whole numbers, locate point 6, a point greater than 6, locate point 9 and one less than 9. Source first line labeled 0,1,2,5,8,9,10; second line labels 0,5,10.
stageA.activity2: Original make-your-own 0..20 number line on a 24–30 inch strip using a repeated physical length unit; mark 3 and 13, compare with partner, ensure uniform adjacent intervals; different unit lengths across students are allowed
stageA.representation: Within a given line tick intervals are equal, sequential, anchored at zero; a marked point identifies a number. Length interval chosen by pupil need not be inches/cm.
stageA.teacherOnly: Notice/wonder oral discourse, physically accurate drawn/constructed number line, 0..20 ticks, partner comparison, teacher evaluation of actual student ruler analogue
stageA.originalCoolDown: Publisher original Cool-down access is restricted; independently authored Edulytics exercise only, no verbatim copyrighted restricted test
stageA.sourceReviewedVia: Live public lesson and preparation pages, not private teacher-login-only materials
stageA.stageAOriginalityBoundary: Use source facts and mathematically original generated exercises; do not invent source images, student discussions, or physical work

baselineAudit.originalExplanation: Identifies number-line structure and earlier rulers, but does not fully teach how units and tick marks represent numbers from zero.
baselineAudit.originalKeyConcepts: Generic locate numbers and broad measurement wording; needs explicit number line versus standard unit distinction.
baselineAudit.originalWorkedExamples: Starts true original tasks but contains truncated ellipsis, and should not be treated as a complete worked solution.
baselineAudit.originalStepByStepSolutions: Five generic steps not grounded in 0..10 equal ticks, 0..20 student construction, 3 and 13 point placement.
baselineAudit.originalCommonMistakes: Generic rather than identifying unequal spacing, shifted zero and incorrect point alignment.
baselineAudit.recommendation: Stage B: source SHA and exact six-field guarded content correction; Stage C: reviewed exact 0..10 missing-tick/point/greater-less and 0..20 equal-unit families, protected student UI, authored tests. Preserve human-only physical modeling. Do not auto-close without B/C.
baselineAudit.evidenceLimit: No compilation, runtime test, CI, Stage D, teacher academic acceptance, merge, or deployment attempted.
